nodes.title: hyprland crashes when I leave the house
nodes.body:
### Hyprland version

v0.56.1

### Is this a regression?

Yes

### What's the bug?

Any time I go away for more than an hour or two I return to find that hyprland has crashed and restarted in a recovery mode.

### Reproduction steps

1. Turn off the monitor.
1. Go out to a nice dinner.
2. Sirloin, medium rare, baked potato with all the fixings.
3. Return.
4. Turn the monitor back on.
5. Sigh.

### I acknowledge that:

- [X] I have searched **all** (open and closed) discussions and issues and my problem is not there.

- [X] I have read the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/hyprwm/.github/blob/main/policies/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) and agree to follow it.

- [X] I wrote this request with my own hands, my own keyboard, and in my own words.

nodes.title: Regression in 0.56: "workspace N silent" window rule applied to a toplevel created during an active tab drag corrupts layout state, SIGSEGV in CDwindleAlgorithm::resizeTarget
nodes.body:
## Hyprland Version

```
Hyprland 0.56.1 built from branch v0.56.1 at commit 5c9377c15f85c50648f35ca5a213754f95b93ca0 clean (version: bump to 0.56.1).
Tag: v0.56.1, commits: 7643

Hyprgraphics: 0.5.1, Hyprutils: 0.14.0, Hyprcursor: 0.1.13, Hyprlang: 0.6.8, Aquamarine: 0.14.0
```

Arch Linux, kernel 6.18.41-1-lts. GPU: Intel Arc A380 (DG2). Dwindle layout, Lua config.

**Regression window:** never happened on 0.55.x (0.55.4 and earlier, in daily use since May). First crash occurred the same day 0.56.0 was installed; reproduces on 0.56.1.

## Bug or Regression Description

I run Chrome instances with custom classes (`--class=jup-chrome` etc.) and had persistent window rules pinning them to workspaces:

```lua
hl.window_rule({
  match = { class = "jup-chrome" },
  workspace = "4 silent",
})
```

With such a rule active, tearing a tab out of a Chrome window (which creates a new toplevel **while the toplevel drag is still active**) breaks the compositor in stages:

1. The torn-out window is immediately moved to the rule's workspace, mid-drag.
2. The window then misbehaves: sometimes it is not rendered at all (invisible), while still present in `hyprctl clients`.
3. The dwindle layout keeps a node for the invisible window. Remaining visible windows can no longer use the full workspace; the ghost node keeps consuming tiling space.
4. A subsequent **mouse-resize** of a tiled window on that workspace segfaults Hyprland.

On 0.55.x the same config and the same action were harmless (the torn-out window would just end up on the pinned workspace after the drag, with no layout corruption).

Removing the persistent `workspace N silent` rules for these classes makes the whole chain (wrong placement, ghost window, crash) disappear. So the trigger is specifically: a window rule with a silent workspace move matching a toplevel that is created during an active xdg toplevel drag.

Even with a "bad" config, the compositor presumably shouldn't end up with a corrupted layout tree and segfault. Either the workspace move should be deferred until the drag ends, or the drag/layout state should survive the move.

## How to Reproduce

1. Dwindle layout, any monitor setup (mine is 3 monitors, workspaces bound per monitor).
2. Add a window rule: class `google-chrome` (or a custom `--class`), `workspace = "N silent"` where N is *not* the current workspace.
3. Open that Chrome instance, several tabs, on its pinned workspace.
4. Drag a tab out of the tab bar to tear it into a new window.
5. Observe the new window jump to another workspace mid-drag; often it stops rendering, and the dwindle tree on the target workspace keeps an invisible node.
6. Mouse-resize (SUPER + right-drag / resize corner) any tiled window on the affected workspace: SIGSEGV.

Crashes within one or two attempts for me.

## Crash Report (backtrace)

Two identical crash reports from consecutive days, both:

```
Hyprland received signal 11(SEGV)
Version: 5c9377c15f85c50648f35ca5a213754f95b93ca0 (v0.56.1)

#7  Layout::CLayoutManager::resizeTarget(...)

#9  CInputManager::mouseMoveUnified(...)
#10 CInputManager::onMouseMoved(IPointer::SMotionEvent)
...
#18 Aquamarine::CSession::handleLibinputEvent(...)
```

nodes.title: Broken dragging behaviour for self-positioning XWayland windows since Hyprland 0.56
nodes.body:
Forwarding verbatim from: https://github.com/audacious-media-player/audacious/issues/1852

**Describe the bug**
Trying to drag Audacious windows causes them to wobble about and sometimes even fly off the screen.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ac08fb17-abca-45fa-bea2-cba772dccd7b

**Steps to reproduce**
Use Hyprland 0.56.0-2 with Audacious in Winamp mode and drag the window. This only started happening after I updated Hyprland.

**Expected behavior**
Normal dragign behaviour.

**Additional information**
* Audacious 4.6.1 (Arch Linux) Winamp
* Arch Linux 6.18.39-1-lts
* Hyprland 0.56.0-2

Nothing shows up in logs after starting it but here they are anyway:
[audacious.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30300854/audacious.log)
